A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PICore work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or reformatted in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original FNO and UNO experiments on four PDE datasets, including prediction errors, training acceleration, coreset diversity, and zero-shot super-resolution results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, convergence and timing analyses, a warm-start ablation, and mixed-resolution experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain physics-informed warm starting, coreset selection, simulation of selected inputs, and supervised training. The losses, finite-difference residual computation, and selection algorithms are unchanged. Mixed-resolution evaluation does not introduce a new PICore procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds mixed-resolution Burgers training with FNO, combining inputs at resolutions 32 and 64. This extends coverage to heterogeneous training grids, distinct from the retained zero-shot higher-resolution evaluations. The four original PDE tasks remain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 add random selection, physics-informed-only training, and an uncertainty-based ensemble active-learning baseline. These resolution-64 comparisons now report one selected supervised algorithm per dataset/operator instead of all five. The k-means, cosine-similarity, and herding comparisons remain in Appendix Figures 4–7.

E3.justification: New experimental designs include active learning initialized with 10% labeled data and ten operators followed by single-step variance-based acquisition, an EL2N/Burgers warm-start sweep over 10/25/50/100 epochs, and equal-sized resolution-32/64 training subsets. The original default 25 warm-up epochs, 500 training epochs, and NRMSE evaluation remain. Newly disclosed dataset sizes do not establish changed splits.

E4.justification: v2 adds warm-start sensitivity testing in Table 9, mixed-resolution analysis in Table 10, convergence comparisons against active learning in Figures 2–3, and training/data-generation/warm-up cost breakdowns in Tables 5–8. The original centroid-distance analysis is retained in Appendix C.2 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 adds uncertainty entries to the main accuracy tables and error bars to the unsupervised-comparison plots, substantially extending uncertainty reporting beyond v1's centroid analysis. Both versions already report averaging over five seeds; no increased run count or new formal significance test is documented. The main tables do not explicitly define their ± quantities.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the new baselines and analyses, while omitting most resolution-64 supervised-selector result rows. Existing full-data values also change: Advection/FNO NRMSE is 2.13e-2 in v1 Table 1 and 2.22e-2 in v2 Table 1. The Section 6.1 example changing from 3.77e-2 to 3.46e-2 instead reflects replacing an across-selector average with the retained graNd result, not improved performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and Appendix B optimization descriptions are retained without substantive changes. No theorem or proof is added. The new centroid-norm explanation clarifies an existing metric rather than introducing new mathematics.

C1.justification: The central claims about label-free selection, architecture/selector modularity, and up to 78% savings remain. The introduction newly characterizes PICore as single-shot active learning and removes the contribution bullet's explicit 5× improvement claim relative to non-coreset training.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for physics-only training failure, convergence relative to active learning, and mixed-resolution behavior. Section 7 newly discusses dependence on a known, differentiable PDE and possible surrogate or weak-form alternatives. Some new interpretations overreach: Appendix C.4 claims consistent mixed-resolution improvements that Table 10 does not support.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 1,000 trajectories per dataset, a 900/100 training/test split, temporal lengths, and baseline implementation details. Conversely, it removes the code link, RTX A4000 hardware statement, and Appendix A's largest-resolution generation/downsampling description. These are documentation changes; actual code availability or changes to retained preprocessing are not established.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning relative to active learning through a dedicated subsection, the single-shot interpretation of PICore, and new discussions of uncertainty sampling, convergence, and time-step acquisition. Added works include Musekamp et al., Haimovich et al., and Kim et al.; these citations do not imply those methods were directly benchmarked.

P1.justification: There are targeted introduction and results rewrites, a new related-work hierarchy, and reorganization of Appendix C, including relocation of the centroid discussion. Much of the background, method, and conclusion retains its wording. The revision also introduces local grammatical errors rather than providing a comprehensive language revision.

P2.justification: Tables 1–4 are extensively redesigned with selected algorithms, new baseline rows, uncertainty entries, and per-row acceleration values. v1 Tables 5–8 become Appendix Figures 4–7, and the centroid figure changes from a horizontal strip to a 2×2 arrangement. New convergence plots, component-cost tables, and ablation/mixed-resolution tables substantially alter the presentation.

improvement.justification: The added controls, uncertainty reporting, and warm-start and cost analyses make the unchanged method easier to assess. The net gain is limited by lost code/hardware information and new reporting problems: Section 6.1 quotes PICore's 20% Navier–Stokes/FNO error as 1.12e-2 although Table 4 reports 1.12e-1, and Appendix C.4 overstates mixed-resolution gains. The additional evidence is useful, but its interpretation needs correction.
